tone_statements.citation: Shehu, Ibrahim Ahmad, Sirajo Muhammad Abubakar & Stephen Jatau. 2023. Tonology of Èlóyì language. International Journal of Arts, Languages, Linguistics and Literary Studies (JOLLS) 12(4): 68-75. ISSN 2636-7149.
tone_statements.quote: There are two types of tone and both are attested in Èlóyì language. These two types of tone are “register, and contour tones.” Register Tones The register tones are the three (3) basic tones known as High (H), Mid (M), and Low (L). [...] Such cases are also obtainable in Èlóyì where three of contour tones are attested. The three contour tones found in Èlóyì are Falling ([F] which results from a glide from high to low tone), Rising ([R] a glide from low to high), and Rising-Falling ([RF] a glide from a low tone to a high, and then to another low). However, these types of tone are of rare occurrence.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 72-73, section 'Data presentation and analysis: Tones in Èlóyì' - 'Register Tones' and 'Contour ones'; findings list p. 75 item iv on the mid tone as possible downstepped high
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 level (H, M, L) + 3 rare contours (F, R, RF); M possibly a downstepped H

sources.citation: Armstrong, Robert G. 1983. The Idomoid languages of the Benue and Cross River valleys. Journal of West African Languages 13(1): 91-149.
sources.note: Nothing on stress (the word does not occur in the 58-page scanned). Typological remarks pp. 97-98: Igede has a four-level register tone system, 'All the other Idomoid languages have three-register systems'; downdrift rare, downstep non-existent; 'With very rare exceptions, all syllables are open. Where noun plurals are distinguished, they always have the same tones as the singular except in Eloyi. There the i-/i- animal class makes a systematic tonal difference in the plural in the Southern or Eloyi Mbeji dialect. In the Northern or Eloyi Mbekyi dialect, singular-plural tone differences occur…

sources.citation: Armstrong, Robert G. 1964. Notes on Etulo; A few more words of Eloyi. Journal of West African Languages 1(2): 57-60.
sources.note: Nothing. The Eloyi part (pp. 59-60) is a supplementary wordlist (Eloyi Mbeci dialect, from a Mr Ekute of Esaari) with tone marks and a duodecimal numeral list; the only phonology statement in the article (three tone levels) is about Etulo, not Eloyi. Scan scanned.

sources.citation: Mackay, Hugh D. 1964. A word-list of Eloyi. Journal of West African Languages 1(1): 5-12.
sources.note: Nothing. Scan scanned. 'PHONEMICS' and 'PROSODIC FEATURES' (pp. 5-6): 'Vowels occasionally occur long (marked :) or overlong (marked ::). There are three levels of tone, high, mid (but usually unmarked in this paper), and low. Very occasionally falling or rising tones occur.' Phonetic note 5: 'All final low tones have an extra low glide.' No mention of stress.

sources.note: Autosegmental description of Eloyi tone from fieldwork word data; three level (register) tones H, M, L, all contrastive on mono-, di- and polysyllables (Tables 1-4); three rare contour tones Falling, Rising, Rising-Falling (Table 5, the RF mostly on the response particles 'nnn', 'èéè'); tonal minimal pairs/sets show lexical and derivational function (Table 6) and tone alone distinguishes sentence types/tense (grammatical function, Table 7); the authors note the mid tone 'sounds like a downstepped high tone' and recommend acoustic study.
sources.venue: International Journal of Arts, Languages, Linguistics and Literary Studies (JOLLS)

sources.note: Database record: the GM inventory for Eloyi lists 51 segments including exactly three tone letters, high ˦, mid ˧ and low ˨ (no contour tonemes), coded from Mackay's WALDS vol. 1 Eloyi data sheet (pp. 194-207) - i.e. the print-only WALDS sheet (a work listed here) records a three-level tone system, consistent with Mackay 1964.
